_about: Pinned result of running the policy-guard/1 conformance corpus (see scripts/policy-guard-corpus.mjs) through the DepositX adapter. Every case NOT listed here AGREES. Reasons are ours. A case that newly diverges, or one that silently starts agreeing, fails test/policy-guard-divergences.test.js: review the change, then edit this file on purpose. This table records differences of design; it is not a defect list and no kernel behaviour was changed to produce agreement.

records/not-an-object.reason: a non-object spend has nothing for the adapter to turn into a signed instruction; DepositX never sees a bare spend

records/null-record.reason: a null spend has nothing for the adapter to turn into a signed instruction; DepositX never sees a bare spend

records/unknown-kind.reason: DepositX has no open kind vocabulary; only transfer-like instruction types exist, so an unknown kind has no counterpart

records/chain-without-family.reason: DepositX is a single ledger with no chain id on a spend, so a malformed chain id cannot be expressed

records/chain-family-uppercase.reason: DepositX is a single ledger with no chain id on a spend, so a malformed chain id cannot be expressed

records/empty-asset.reason: DepositX has exactly one asset and no asset field on an instruction, so an empty asset cannot be expressed

records/swap-with-destination.reason: DepositX has no swap kind (CONVERT and DvP exist but can never be granted to an agent)

records/amount-leading-zeros.reason: real difference: DepositX amounts are canonical decimal strings with no leading zeros (the string is inside the signed digest), so 0050 is refused where the other engine reads it as 50

records/amount-zero.reason: real difference: DepositX refuses a zero-cent transfer as a malformed amount; the other engine treats zero as a valid, under-cap spend

envelopes/envelope-for-another-chain.reason: a grant is per issuer on one ledger; there is no per-chain envelope to miss

envelopes/kind-not-permitted.reason: the record kind (bridge) has no DepositX counterpart, so the allowed-kinds check cannot be exercised

envelopes/asset-not-permitted.reason: DepositX has one asset and no asset allowlist on a grant

envelopes/asset-matches-case-insensitive.reason: DepositX has one asset and no asset allowlist on a grant

envelopes/destination-matches-case-insen.reason: DepositX counterparties are exact account ids; whether two address spellings are one account is the adapter address book's call, not the kernel's

envelopes/swap-skips-the-destination-all.reason: DepositX has no swap kind, so the no-destination exemption has no counterpart

caps/per-tx-cap-beyond-double-precision.reason: the envelope needs a 20-digit daily cap; DepositX amounts stop at 18 digits (the kernel refuses the grant), so the precision edge cannot be reached

ceiling/always-escalate-overrides-the-ce.reason: a grant has no ask-every-time flag; per_instruction_max must be positive, so "always escalate" has no counterpart

envelope-shape/envelope-not-an-object.reason: a non-object envelope has nothing the adapter can turn into a GRANT payload

envelope-shape/chain-missing.reason: a DepositX grant has no chain field, so a missing chain cannot be expressed

records/transfer-without-destination.reason: real difference, caused by hardening X1: signatures and the grant's envelope are checked before any account lookup (so an unauthenticated caller cannot probe which accounts exist), so a transfer with no destination is refused by the grant's counterparty list before the kernel notices the destination is not an account

envelopes/no-envelope.reason: real difference, caused by hardening X1: a signature naming a grant that does not exist is BAD_SIGNATURE, identical to a wrong key on a real grant, so a caller who cannot sign cannot enumerate grant ids; the other engine answers NO_ENVELOPE

agreements_to_read_with_care.caps/per-tx-cap-exact: agrees (ESCALATE): 1000 equals the hard per-transaction cap, which is allowed at the cap, and is above the soft ceiling of 100, so the institution must co-sign
agreements_to_read_with_care.caps/daily-cap-exact: agrees (ESCALATE): used-today plus 500 lands exactly on the hard daily cap, which is allowed, and 500 is above the soft ceiling of 100, so the institution must co-sign
